description: A driver chip that sits between the microcontroller and a bipolar stepper motor, converting simple STEP/DIR pulses into the motor's coil currents.
how_to_use: STEP (one pulse = one step) and DIR (0=CCW, 1=CW) are the two pins the microcontroller normally drives. ENABLE (active low, pulled down already)/SLEEP (active low, pulled up)/RESET (active low, floating — must be held high) are usually left at their defaults; MS1/MS2/MS3 select microstepping resolution. VDD/GND are logic power; VMOT is motor power (unused in simulation). 1A/1B connect to the motor's B coil, 2A/2B to the motor's A coil (the driver's '1'/'2' numbering doesn't match the motor's A/B naming — verified from docs, not a typo).

plain.what: A driver board that gives a stepper motor the power it needs, so the Arduino just says 'step' and 'which way'.
plain.how: STEP and DIR to two Arduino pins, the motor's 4 wires to 1A/1B/2A/2B, and a separate power supply to VMOT.
